visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A large orange-golden mineral cluster with sharp, pointed crystals, identified as Dogtooth Calcite, is presented on a dark wooden stand. The background is pitch black, and warm studio spotlights highlight the faceted texture and translucency of the crystals. (2) The camera performs a slow zoom towards the center of the specimen, focusing on the intricate, sharp points and the amber-like color depth of the mineral. (3) The lighting environment switches from visible light to ultraviolet (UV) light. The entire mineral cluster begins to fluoresce, emitting a bright, vibrant yellow-green glow that contrasts sharply with the black background. (4) The camera pans across the specimen while it is under UV illumination, showing the consistent intensity of the fluorescence across different crystal facets. (5) The UV light source is removed, revealing the specimen's phosphorescent properties as it continues to emit a faint, lingering yellow glow in the dark before slowly fading. (6) A handheld light source or pointer highlights specific sections of the cluster, creating moving spots of bright luminescence. (7) The video concludes with a medium shot of the mineral specimen under normal lighting as graphic overlays appear.
